hypothesis: Continuous monotone lane families and cached affine active sets can replace repeated local geometric search on common order types, including mixed-layer endpoint pairs with a central via ladder.
mechanism: Transform lane targets t[i] to t[i]-i*d, solve bounded isotonic least squares using pool-adjacent-violators, and compile its active blocks into affine lane formulas. Cached blocks are instantiated only after fresh block-order, prefix-residual KKT and current bound-mode inequalities pass. A changed parameter domain runs the continuous solve and compiles another template; this is a parameterized solver rather than a finite elbow/chord/site catalog.
template_key: Collective templates are keyed by orientation, ordered endpoint-layer pattern and the copper-versus-drill spacing branch. Numerical coordinates, dimensions, separation and bounds are current parameters and are certified on every use. Single-pair x/y projection templates have separate keys; committed single-pair and collective cells are reported separately.
causal_limit: Both the raw PAV solve and one cached-template domain validation are O(n). This experiment tests the constructive family plus active-set reuse as a package. A gain over native routing cannot establish a causal benefit from caching without the same constructor with caching disabled. Such an ablation is justified remotely only if this package first shows a meaningful gain. Trying several stored domains can cost more than a fresh solve.
domain: Equal native routing traceWidth, exactly two ports per connection. Collective cells require matching order across two opposite faces; endpoints may change layers. Single-pair cells can use different faces. True coordinates, including small mesh-port overhang, are retained with normal inward leads. Physical predicates may reject an otherwise algebraically eligible family. No endpoint, physical budget or topology identity is altered.
physical_profile: The via pitch is max(annulus diameter plus foreign-copper clearance, actual caller viaHoleDiameter plus actual drill-edge clearance), with a numerical guard. The P9 factory passes actual CMS drill diameter and SRJ hole/pad rules. Same-net distinct drills still obey the hole gap; exact same-net XY site reuse is allowed. Vias are explicitly unsupported when a fixed/preloaded routing scene has incomplete drill metadata. No assumption that annulus diameter alone protects an unusually large drill gap is made.
scene_certificate: Independent Euclidean copper tests cover wires, via spans, all original endpoints, actual nearby scene ports, rotated/circular obstacles and board outline. Canonical registered electrical ownership allows wire contact with owned pads; aliases cannot exempt foreign pads, and via/pad and nonplated-hole exclusions remain. Candidates wait while native cells finish. Updated fixed copper, actual native copper and other pending families are rechecked before commit, including drill-to-drill distance; any rejected pending family dispatches to unchanged native routing and the remaining scene is checked again.
scope_limits: This is a bounded monotone family, not an arbitrary planar embedding or general variable-width simultaneous router. Fan geometry can fail independent Euclidean spacing even when ordered lane constraints fit. Routing traceWidth is the same nominal input used by native HD; final per-net widening, length matching, simplification and repair remain downstream and unchanged. Fixed/preloaded drill scenes exclude via construction. Global scene certification uses serial HD scheduling, including solveAsync.
work_removed: Committed cells do not instantiate regular HD search. Counters distinguish attempts, geometric eligibility, pending invalidation, committed single/collective families, constructed routes/vias, raw continuous solves, block merges, compiled templates, cache hits, domain failures, physical predicates and native cells. Constructor scene-index setup time is exposed because the existing HD phase timer starts after construction. End-to-end elapsed time is primary.
falsifiers: Low committed coverage on expensive cells prevents a 10x end-to-end gain, regardless of counts of cheap single-pair hits
Template-domain search, physical certificates, index setup or serial scheduling cost more than the native search removed
Mixed-layer fan or via geometry is usually rejected, or later native copper invalidates the accepted family
Downstream quality repairs or widening consume the saved work
Any strict final board quality regression rejects this implementation
validation: Independent exhaustive active-partition oracle for bounded isotonic objectives, spacing and bounds
Translated continuous three-wire mixed-layer families: real endpoint overhang, active-block reuse and changed-domain rejection; explicit wire-wire, via-wire and via-via clearance assertions
Actual large hole-edge gap changes the pitch and feasibility domain; unknown drill rules/scenes are excluded; distinct same-net drills and exact-site reuse are tested
Rotated/circular obstacles, blind versus through-via foreign ports, board outline and canonical electrical-ownership collisions
Phase integration separates single/collective commits from attempted templates and verifies zero regular node searches for two accepted mixed-layer families
Controlled later native drill invalidates a pending family even when copper clearance is satisfied
Unmodified existing P9 fixture activates both single and collective construction and passes independent final copper/endpoint checks
Existing differential-pair length and pad-clearance regression, TypeScript check and package build
performance_claim: None before paired Blacksmith results. Cell coverage is not time-weighted CPU coverage. A negative result applies to this implementation and eligibility domain, not every possible microcompiler.
